title: Physics
blurb: Energy, heat and waves in everyday life.

lessons.title: Energy & heat
lessons.summary: Where energy goes, how heat moves, and why heat pumps beat heaters.

cards.title: Energy changes form
cards.text:
Energy is never created or destroyed, only converted. A battery's chemical energy becomes electrical energy, which a bulb turns into light and heat.

Efficiency is the useful share. An old filament bulb turned about 5% into light; an LED manages several times that, so it runs cooler for the same brightness.

cards.title: Three ways heat moves
cards.text:
Conduction: heat passes through touching material, from the burner into the pan base.
Convection: warm fluid rises and cool fluid sinks, setting up loops that stir the water.
Radiation: infrared light travels across a gap with no material at all, like the warmth you feel beside a fire.

cards.title: Heat pumps move heat
cards.text:
A heat pump doesn't make heat; it moves it. A refrigerant absorbs heat from outside air (even cold air has some), the compressor squeezes it so it gets hotter, and it releases that heat indoors.

Because most of the heat comes from outside, 1 kWh of electricity can deliver 3–4 kWh of heat. That ratio is the COP.

cards.title: Specific heat
cards.text: The energy to heat something is mass × specific heat × temperature rise. Water's specific heat is high, about 4186 J per kg per °C, which is why it takes a while to boil and why it stores heat so well.

quiz.q: Which way does heat mainly reach you from the Sun?
quiz.explain: Space is nearly empty, so only radiation can cross it.

quiz.q: A heat pump with a COP of 3 uses 2 kWh of electricity. Heat delivered?
quiz.explain: Heat out = COP × electricity in = 3 × 2 = 6 kWh.

lessons.title: Waves, sound & light
lessons.summary: One equation that covers guitar strings, Wi-Fi and thunderstorms.

cards.title: Anatomy of a wave
cards.text: A wave carries energy without carrying stuff along. Its wavelength (λ) is the distance from one crest to the next. Its amplitude is how tall it is, which sets loudness or brightness. Its frequency is how many crests pass each second, in hertz (Hz).

cards.title: Try it: how long is a sound?
cards.text: Speed equals frequency times wavelength. Sound travels at about 343 m/s in air, so low notes have long waves and high notes have short ones.

cards.title: How far away is the storm?
cards.text:
Light from lightning reaches you almost instantly; it travels about 300 000 km every second. Sound crawls along at about 343 m/s, roughly 1 km every 3 seconds.

Count the seconds between the flash and the thunder and divide by 3 to get the distance in kilometres.

cards.title: The electromagnetic spectrum
cards.text:
Radio, microwaves, infrared, visible light, ultraviolet and X-rays are all the same thing: electromagnetic waves, all moving at the speed of light. Only the wavelength differs.

Shorter waves carry more energy per photon. That's why UV can burn skin and X-rays pass through it, while radio is harmless. Wi-Fi at 2.4 GHz has a wavelength of about 12.5 cm.

quiz.q: A 343 Hz tone in air (343 m/s) has a wavelength of…
Thunder arrives 9 seconds after the flash. How far is the strike?
quiz.explain: Sound covers about 1 km every 3 s, so 9 s ≈ 3 km.

quiz.q: Which carries the most energy per photon?
quiz.explain: Shorter wavelength means higher frequency and more energy per photon.
